GET …/map/{layer}.geojson
one row per selected layer · a degraded row says why
What this is

Per-layer metadata: source status, freshness, attribution, and the absolute .geojson URL a third-party map client would point at.

It is why a consumer can trust — or knows not to trust — what the map shows.

A failed layer is loud

A degraded row is tinted and says which failure in words underneath. Nothing on the map is never an all-clear — an UNAVAILABLE layer draws nothing, and that is a different statement from a layer that drew nothing because there was nothing to draw.

Unlocated features

Features with "geometry": null — e.g. a county-wide advisory — are valid and can't be drawn on the map, so they are listed here instead (never dropped).
